title: the night plan follows the tier

findings.claim: the night chain wrote the tier's pass order, concurrency and residency into MICROBATCH options the worker never reads; the tests stopped at the options
findings.expected: the plan states only steps a job runs and writes no option
findings.happened: options passes, screen_concurrency, models_resident on the job; the worker ran its usual evaluation

findings.claim: a coded-only plan still dispatched the ordinary MICROBATCH, which can ask the configured note judge
findings.expected: no coded-only claim the screen step does not keep; a record measuring no model is warned as differing from the configuration
findings.happened: models_on_card none stated while MICROBATCH could send notes to the judge

findings.claim: the 06:00 CPU note cutoff cancelled jobs, then advanced the chain with CPU note dispatch still on
findings.expected: no job is started or cancelled by the plan
findings.happened: a fresh night_pass=note_cpu job could start in the backup window

findings.claim: the cutoff searched only the 200 newest jobs of every type
findings.expected: no cutoff (no job runs a CPU note pass)
findings.happened: a note job behind 200 newer jobs was never cancelled

findings.claim: the backup window wrote no request on the shipped Compose, which mounts no operations folder in the orchestrator
findings.expected: the scheduler opens no backup window it cannot start
findings.happened: the day was marked handled with no request written

findings.claim: the plan read gb10.json and cpu.json for labels the worker's budget lookup does not know: the stated budget differed from the enforced one
findings.expected: one reader and one budget on every label
findings.happened: TB_PROFILE=P-GB10 with a gb10.json of 750: 750 stated, 2000 enforced

findings.claim: two first-load slices had the same name and the second depended on that name
